ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized representatives and agent signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists, Interpol Red Notices, FIC and POCDATARA domestic terrorism lists, CIPC disqualified-director register under s 69 of the Companies Act, and reputable commercial KYC databases. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence and senior management approval before incorporation proceeds; ongoing transaction and relationship monitoring must be implemented under FICA ss 20A–24.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC Online Transacting System / e-Services portal (www.cipc.co.za) — Name Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be expressed in any of the 11 South African official languages or in a transliteration, but must be written in Roman/Latin alphabetic characters. Names using non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet. The name must not be offensive, obscene, misleading, calculated to cause offence, or falsely imply official patronage, government connection, professional licensing, or unlawful purposes. Names that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, close corporation, trade mark, or reserved name are rejected. Legal-form suffixes must comply with the Companies Act: a private company must carry the suffix (Pty) Ltd.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names implying terrorist or money-laundering connections
Names reproducing registered trade marks or protected state heraldry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The incorporator must submit CIPC Form CoR 9.1 (or the online name-reservation application) with up to four ranked alternative names. If CIPC issues a rejection notice, the applicant may (1) file a new reservation application through the CIPC portal with corrected alternatives; (2) submit a written reconsideration request to CIPC within 20 business days of rejection, specifying the statutory ground and attaching supporting proof; (3) apply to the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act for an order directing CIPC to reserve the name in cases of unreasonable administrative refusal or similarity disputes; and (4) review the Tribunal or Commission decision in the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000. Administrative reconsideration normally resolves within 10–20 business days; judicial review may take 6–12 months. A reserved name that expires before formal incorporation requires a fresh reservation; renewal may be sought within the prescribed statutory discretion before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for Companies Act purposes provided the virtual-office provider supplies a physical street address in South Africa (not a post-office box), can accept service of process, and maintains business-hours document-access arrangements. A virtual office will not satisfy municipal business-premises and food-safety licensing for a ghost kitchen; the delivery-only kitchen itself must have a separately licensed physical kitchen address under the Foodstuffs, Cosmetics and Disinfectants Act 54 of 1972 and applicable municipal by-laws.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate, approximately 35% for CIPC/FIC registered-office and records inspections for a low-risk standard private company; materially higher, approximately 70–80%, for municipal environmental-health and food-safety inspections at the actual ghost-kitchen operating site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 13(1), 14, 15 and 19; Companies Regulations, 2011, Forms CoR 14.1 and CoR 14.2
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) incorporating the Memorandum of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Proprietary Limited company; the MOI sets authorised capital, and no escrow or capital-deposit account is required under the Companies Act 71 of 2008
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company be approved and the Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation as signed be filed; that the subscription for 100 ordinary shares of ZAR1 each by the subscribers be accepted, that such shares be allotted fully paid in cash; that the registered office be at [address]; that [Name] be appointed sole Director, that [Name] be appointed CEO and [Name] be appointed Company Secretary; that the directors be authorised to open bank accounts, appoint legal counsel, negotiate the lease of the ghost-kitchen premises, and execute all ancillary documents; that notification of appointment in respect of the Director and Company Secretary be filed as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access CIPC e-Services, submit the corporate name reservation application with two proposed distinctive names, and confirm the name does not contain prohibited material under the Companies Regulations. Complete the reservation before the incorporation filing; the reservation is valid for 6 months and may be extended once.
required_dossiers: Second and third preferred name alternatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused, file an administrative reconsideration within 20 business days of refusal, or select an alternative name and resubmit; the CIPC must be notified of the correction before the expiry of the reserved period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI specifying share classes, voting rights, director powers, and quorum provisions; complete Form CoR 14.1. Have each incorporator execute the MOI and the Notice of Incorporation. Notarisation is not ordinarily required unless an authorised agent signs under power of attorney.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC queries the MOI due to inconsistent or incomplete provisions, file a revised CoR 14.1 or MOI addendum through the CIPC corrections channel before the statutory compliance deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application and payment of regulatory fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the CIPC e-Services portal, select 'New Company Registration', upload the signed CoR 14.1 and MOI, pay the prescribed incorporation fee by card or electronic deposit, and retain the automated submission reference number.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 signed by all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for a defect or inconsistency, correct the relevant form and resubmit within 20 business days after CIPC's notification; a correctly completed application is not charged again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and verification of entity particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once CIPC approves the application, the company is allocated a registration number and a computerised Certificate of Incorporation is issued. Download and print the certificate from the CIPC e-Services portal and verify that the legal name, registration number, and date of incorporation match the filed MOI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a typographical or an administrative error appears on the certificate, apply for amendment and correction through the CIPC amendments module; no new incorporation application is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of first board meeting and appointment of governance officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to adopt the first board resolution, appoint directors, officers, and the company secretary, approve the bank mandate, and adopt a resolution for the subsequent lease and trade licences. File the prescribed notices of director and officer appointments, and maintain the MOI and statutory records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
First board resolution on issued shares
Share certificates for the initial subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC rejects the filing of director particulars due to an omitted consent form, obtain the missing consent and resubmit through the CIPC service request function without altering the effective appointment date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Department of Health and the local municipal Environmental Health Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Acceptability for Food Premises under section 10 of the Foodstuffs, Cosmetics and Disinfectants Act 52 of 1972 and the General Hygiene Regulations for Food Premises (R638)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Affairs (through the provincial environmental affairs authority and municipal licensing desk)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration and exemption screening under the listing notices of NEMA 1998; a Full EIA is not required for a standard multi-brand cloud kitchen unless the activity involves significant cold-storage ammonia volumes, diesel generator capacity above threshold, or discharge of industrial effluent requiring a Water Use Licence
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater containing oil and grease must be treated via grease traps before discharge; typical municipal standard is less than 10 mg/L oil and grease, with pH 6–11 and suspended solids within local municipality sewer by-laws. Cooking exhaust must include particulate extraction and VOC abatement to meet National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 thresholds, and solid waste must be segregated and disposed in accordance with NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire department covering automatic commercial-cooking suppression systems, extinguishers, exit signage, and monthly inspections; structural load inspections from the local building control department for mezzanine and racking installations; occupational workplace clearance under OHSA 85 of 1993 including an electrical Certificate of Compliance and registration of the workplace with the Department of Employment and Labour for COIDA.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); online operational portal at SARS eFiling – https://www.sarsefiling.co.za, with authoritative legal and procedural information published at https://www.sars.gov.za.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident owned South African private company (Pty) Ltd: (1) incorporate through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) and obtain a certificate of incorporation; (2) appoint a public officer who is ordinarily resident in South Africa under s 246 of the Tax Administration Act; (3) register for income tax and VAT via SARS eFiling or at a SARS branch by submitting the prescribed registration forms, including the company income tax registration form (and for VAT, VAT 101); supporting documents required comprise CIPC registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of the public officer's appointment and identity, proof of the company's physical and postal addresses (including a South African address for a foreign registered company), and, for non-resident VAT vendors, a local representative agreement; (4) SARS issues an income tax reference number and, after VAT registration, a separate VAT vendor registration number; (5) maintain updated registered particulars and file returns as required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no check-the-box or general hybrid-entity classification election for companies. A (Pty) Ltd is automatically a separate taxpayer liable on worldwide income at the 27% corporate rate. Elective options affecting tax profile include: small business corporation status under s 12E for qualifying South African-resident companies with turnover below R20 million; s 11D research and development allowance claims; s 12J venture capital company investment elections; financial instruments held may be aligned to tax under s 8E. Hybrid mismatch interest deductions are governed by ss 8F–8M and controlled foreign company rules; these operate automatically with no elective override. A foreign company may appoint a representative taxpayer under the Act, but entity classification remains based on domestic law and not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration arises when taxable supplies in South Africa exceed R1,000,000 (one million South African Rand) in any consecutive 12-month period; registration must be applied for within 21 business days. Voluntary VAT registration is possible if taxable supplies exceed R50,000. Foreign suppliers of electronic services, including delivery-interface and app-based services, are similarly required to register and charge VAT where supplies exceed the R1 million threshold. Non-established suppliers must use SARS eFiling and may be required to appoint a local representative and provide security for VAT obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or automated e-invoicing clearance at the point of sale. Tax invoices meeting s 20 of the VAT Act (electronic or paper) must be issued for taxable supplies and must include five-yearly prescribed particulars. Electronic tax invoices are accepted if performance and accuracy can be proved by normal data-processing procedures. SARS has deployed e@syFile and eFiling for VAT administrative and clearance purposes, and data is transmitted through the VAT 201 return. SARS may use automated analytics and Smart Audit to query invoice data, but there is no live tax-authority pre-clearance requirement before a document can be used.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for goods applies under s 11(3) of the VAT Act where the goods are supplied to a non-resident and are consigned to a destination outside South Africa, provided the supplier retains the prescribed documentary evidence of export. For services, s 11(2) zero-rates a supply of services to a non-resident for use wholly or partially in a foreign country, subject to exceptions such as services connected to South African land or movable property. For a ghost kitchen business, local meal sales and delivery are standard-rated; zero-rating may apply strictly to separately chargeable offshore services (e.g., management or head-office support supplied to an overseas group company) where the beneficial use is outside South Africa and proper evidence of foreign settlement is maintained. All zero-rated export transactions will be examined at audit to ensure actual payment in foreign currency and physical export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD 500/SCC) bearing a unique movement reference number (UMRN) and confirming SARS Customs release to the exporter
Commercial invoice together with the original combined transport bill of lading or air waybill evidencing the consignment to a destination outside South Africa

Inward remittance certificate (IRC) or foreign exchange settlement certificate issued by an authorised South African bank, proving receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency within the statutory period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If a zero-rating claim is not substantiated, SARS may recharacterise the supply as taxable under s 15(1), raising an assessment for VAT, interest and penalties. Under the Tax Administration Act, understatement penalties range from 10% for substantial non-disclosure with no reasonable grounds to 200% for intentional tax evasion. SARS may extend the general five-year audit prescription to ten years for non-disclosure or fraudulent conduct. Deliberately false export declarations constitute a criminal offence under both the VAT Act and the Customs and Excise Act, with prospective imprisonment of up to five years and personal liability for directors if SARS can establish negligence or fraud. A retrospective clawback of VAT refunds may be made for all affected tax periods, and SARS is not bound by previous refund allocations if the export claim is discredited. A section 204 TAA voluntary disclosure arrangement may mitigate penalties only if submitted before infection.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the statutory exchange-control authority and through the Prudential Authority as the banking supervisor under the Banks Act, 1990 (Act 94 of 1990). All foreign-exchange transactions are executed by commercial banks in their capacity as Authorized Dealers in foreign exchange under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The rand (ZAR) is freely convertible for current-account transactions: trade in goods, food-and-beverage imports, kitchen-equipment purchases, SaaS subscriptions, and delivery-platform commissions payable offshore are permitted through an Authorized Dealer without SARB pre-approval, provided the bank holds the underlying invoice, contract, and the correct balance-of-payments purpose code. Capital-account inflows from non-residents (equity subscription by foreign shareholders of ZA_PTY_LTD) are unrestricted and do not require FinSurv consent, but the inward transfer must be recorded with an Authorized Dealer in the inward investment register to preserve the legal ability to remit dividends and repay shareholder loans. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted once the foreign capital was formally introduced, the annual financial statements are prepared, SARS tax clearance is presented, and the 20% Dividends Tax is withheld or reduced under an applicable double-taxation treaty. Practical hurdles are documentary rather than quantitative: the bank requires proof of the foreign investment inflow, a signed distribution declaration, and evidence that the company is in good standing with CIPC and SARS. Capital-account outflows by residents remain restricted; therefore all outbound treasury flows must be rationalised as current-account items (trade or service payments) and never as offshore deposits or unapproved investments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Delivery-format food service revenue is classified as an export of services when the counterparty or settlement entity is a non-resident (for example, DoorDash US settling USD for virtual-brand access on the US platform). All export service proceeds must be repatriated to South Africa and credited to an Authorized Dealer account within 180 calendar days of the invoice or service-completion date. No fixed statutory percentage must be converted to ZAR; proceeds may be retained in a Foreign Currency Account only up to the amount required for identifiable, near-term foreign disbursements, with the surplus sold to the dealing bank at the ruling spot rate. The exporter must lodge an Export Declaration for Services (Form S) or the bank's digital export module, supported by marketplace settlement statements and order-level reports. Non-compliance triggers an irregular-export report to FinSurv, which may result in administrative penalties, withdrawal of forward-exchange facilities, and adverse scoring in the bank's AML/CFT file. Domestic UberEats South Africa settlements in ZAR from Uber's local contracting entity are outside the surrender regime but must still be reconcilable in the company's VAT 201 return and management accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dual-structure: Capital Escrow Account (inward foreign investment in ZAR/USD) + Operational Business Account (ZAR daily clearing)
Business Current Account (ZAR) with supplementary Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR/GBP) for marketplace receivables

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium-High as an auxiliary receivable-collection rail, but Low as a primary treasury concentration point. Under the National Payment System Act, 1998 (Act 78 of 1998), offshore Electronic Money Institutions (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Nium) are not licensed Authorized Dealers and may not originate or receive ZAR settlement directly from South African residents. They can be used as an ancillary collection sidecar for foreign-currency marketplace vouchers (e.g., DoorDash US payouts), but the Foreign Currency Account must be declared as an offshore-holding, funds must be swept back to the domestic Authorized Dealer at least monthly, and the FIC will require full transparency of the EMI's beneficial ownership. The sanctioned structure for ZA_PTY_LTD is a domestic bank multi-currency account with SWIFT sweeps rather than an offshore EMI ledger.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (Act 38 of 2001) does not mandate physical appearance where an electronic KYC solution is in place; however, predominant market practice among Tier-1 banks requires at least one Responsible Person (director or authorised signatory) to complete an identity verification step in person, either at a branch or through a bank-branded digital signing service with liveness/OCR. Non-resident directors are accommodated through video KYC plus apostilled passport copies, a banker's reference, and independent sanctions screening; no embassy legalisation is required given South Africa's Hague Apostille Convention membership. A corporate shareholder must provide a certified board resolution authorizing the investment, and an individual shareholder must provide a notarised source-of-wealth declaration. There is no statutory minimum capital for a (Pty) Ltd, but banks may impose a minimum initial deposit of ZAR 100 to ZAR 500 for account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign beneficial owner holding 100% of the issued shares with no local operational track record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register extract identifying all natural persons with direct or indirect ownership of 5% or more; certified copy of the Memorandum of Incorporation; shareholder's notarised source-of-wealth statement supported by three months of home-bank statements; banker's reference from the investor's institution; signed non-PEP declaration; and sanctions-screening confirmation via WorldCheck or equivalent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-brand and ghost-kitchen trading names not matching the registered legal name ZA_PTY_LTD
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed UberEats and DoorDash master-merchant agreements naming ZA_PTY_LTD as the operating merchant and listing all virtual-brand trade names; trademark registration or pending applications in class 43; the kitchen facility lease agreement; municipal Certificate of Acceptability; fire and health permits; and platform menu screenshots establishing the operating reality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity settlement volumes and rapid drawdown of the operating account after an inbound capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving capital deployment; integrated 12-month cash-flow forecast; invoices for kitchen fit-out and equipment; supplier delivery notes; VAT reconciliation; SARS tax clearance; and a low-risk AML tier confirmation for ISIC 5610 delivery-only cloud kitchen operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the company's registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty per CIPC tariff; if not filed within 90 days, CIPC marks the company as 'delinquent' and may initiate administrative strike-off (deregistration) after due process

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the company's financial year-end, or the date SARS prescribes in the notice of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% underpayment penalty plus interest at SARS prescribed rate on unpaid taxes; criminal prosecution for repeated non-submission; SARS may issue a default assessment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit under Companies Act 71 of 2008 if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or higher. PIS is calculated based on average employees, turnover (in millions of ZAR), and third-party liabilities (in millions of ZAR). Private companies with PIS below 350 may be exempt if shareholders approve an independent review instead of a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs as adopted by the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants (SAICA); financial statements must conform to the Companies Act and IFRS frameworks

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act, 2022, the company must maintain a register of beneficial owners and file any changes with CIPC within 30 days. On or before the annual return filing date, the directors must confirm that the register is accurate and up to date; a specific annual confirmation is filed with the annual return.
